title: Cohort Escrow Cutover Queue (CECQ): deferred cutover + auto-prune for safe shadow->canary promotions
author: Lina Morales
description:
Motivation: we continue to see noisy instant promotes from shadow to canary during periods of transient load or metric spikes. This PR introduces a Cohort Escrow Cutover Queue (CECQ) that defers cutovers for a short ledgered window, runs a lightweight rehearsal (synthetic smoke), and automatically prunes stale or conflicting promotions. Goals: reduce accidental rollouts, improve safety for multi-cohort experiments (A/B), and provide auditable crediting so teams can recover for false-positive smoke failures.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a cutover queue that serializes promotions per-cohort with lease-backed escrow so multiple promos for the same user-slice don't race.
- Runs a configurable synthetic-smoke rehearsal before promotion (dry-run traffic routed to a sandbox kernel).
- Implements a rollback-credit ledger: failed rehearsals decrement a credit; when credits are exhausted, promotion is blocked and a dryback policy runs (quarantine + replayable snapshot).
- Auto-prune policy removes stuck entries older than a retention TTL and emits audit events for manual forensic replay.
- Exposes new rollout-config knobs: escrow_ttl_ms, rehearsal_sample_pct, credit_window, prune_policy.
- Adds observability: per-promo telemetry, histograms for rehearsal latency, audit logs, and a new console view to inspect pending escrows.

Checklist (tested locally / CI):
- [x] Unit tests for escrow queue serialization and ledger accounting
- [x] Integration smoke harness that runs synthetic rehearsal against local sandbox runtime
- [x] E2E in perf-canary lab with small cohort (10k requests) to validate no regression in median latency
- [x] Migration path: default to disabled in config; feature flag rollout to canary teams first

Notes on behavior and regression handling:
- The cutover queue is conservative by default (rehearsal_sample_pct=0.05) and does not increase global latency because rehearsals are sampled and run on an isolated execution pool.
- If rehearsal fails transiently but the policy determines signal is noisy (elasticity threshold), the ledger will not penalize credits — this is a safety heuristic implemented in the signal analyzer.
- All promotions are auditable and replayable via the new /internal/rollouts/escrow API endpoints (read-only for default RBAC).

Related Linear items: ENG-1459 (CECQ design), PM-88 (console surface), ENG-1890 (audit retention update).

Potential follow-ups (future PRs):
- Automated credit replenishment strategies tied to historical stability windows
- Console controls for manual bailouts (force-prune / force-promote) with two-person approval

Migration & rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag: rollout.cecq.enabled=false by default.
2) Enable on internal canary orgs for two weeks.
3) Gradual enable for orgs with rollout budgets and observability configured.

Backwards compatibility: the system acts as a noop when the flag is off. There is a one-time migration that creates ledger buckets for active cohorts; migration is idempotent.

Contact: Lina Morales (@lina) for questions or runbook; Rajiv Nair for safety review.

review_comments: Rajiv Nair: Can we reduce rehearsal_sample_pct default to 1% for large orgs? Concerned about hidden cost; suggestion: keep 5% for canary only and 1% for org-level defaults.
Lina Morales: Updated config and added org-level override; docs updated to suggest conservative defaults. See commit: config knobs update.
Sofia Kim: Signal analyzer looks good, but observed potential for credit starvation during multi-arm experiments. Recommend an emergency bypass (manual reset) exposed to SRE team.

release_notes: Introduce Cohort Escrow Cutover Queue (CECQ): deferred promotions with rehearsal, rollback-credit ledger, and auto-prune policy. Disabled by default behind feature flag. Adds observability and console inspection for pending escrows.
